s: 我没是坐火车去的。
s_py: wǒ méi shì zuò huǒ chē qù de
zh: 我不是坐火车去的。
py: wǒ bù shì zuò huǒ chē qù de
en: I did not go by train.
why: 是 is negated with 不, never 没. 没是 does not exist even though the event is in the past.

s: 他们是在公园的见面。
s_py: tā men shì zài gōng yuán de jiàn miàn
zh: 他们是在公园见面的。
py: tā men shì zài gōng yuán jiàn miàn de
en: They met in the park.
why: 的 never goes before the verb. It closes the verb phrase after 见面.

src_py: wǒ zuó tiān shì zuò huǒ chē qù de
task: Say it as a plan for tomorrow.
zh: 我明天坐火车去。
py: wǒ míng tiān zuò huǒ chē qù
en: I am going by train tomorrow.
why: Tomorrow has not happened, so 是…的 gives way to plain word order. The time word may sit before or after the subject.

q: 我是在上海学___中文的。
zh: 我是在上海学中文的。
py: wǒ shì zài shàng hǎi xué zhōng wén de
en: I studied Chinese in Shanghai.
why: With a noun object, 的 goes either right after the verb or at the end, never both. Here 的 is already at the end, so a second one after 学 is wrong.

s: 他们不是去年搬来的，是今年春天搬来的。
s_py: tā men bù shì qù nián bān lái de shì jīn nián chūn tiān bān lái de
zh: 他们不是去年搬来的，是今年春天搬来的。
py: tā men bù shì qù nián bān lái de shì jīn nián chūn tiān bān lái de
en: They did not move here last year; they moved here this spring.
why: This is correct. Both clauses are 是…的, one negated with 不是. The negation denies the time, not the move.

zh: 我昨天到的。
py: wǒ zuó tiān dào de
en: I arrived yesterday.
why: With 是 dropped the sentence is 我昨天到的; 的 stays and the time word can open the sentence. Without 的 it would be a different sentence about nothing in particular.

s: 这件衣服是昨天买的。
s_py: zhè jiàn yī fu shì zuó tiān mǎi de
zh: 这件衣服是昨天买的。
py: zhè jiàn yī fu shì zuó tiān mǎi de
en: This piece of clothing was bought yesterday.
why: This is correct. The clothing is visible, so only the time is new, and 是…的 is used instead of 了. It may look like a past sentence missing 了, but it is not.

zh: 我是上个星期天在超市门口遇到邻居的。
py: wǒ shì shàng ge xīng qī tiān zài chāo shì mén kǒu yù dào lín jū de
en: I ran into a neighbour at the supermarket entrance last Sunday.
why: 是 sits before the stressed time or place, and 的 closes the clause. If the time word moves to the front, 是 shifts to the place; it can never come after the verb.

s: 你是什么时候搬来的吗？
s_py: nǐ shì shén me shí hou bān lái de ma
zh: 你是什么时候搬来的？
py: nǐ shì shén me shí hou bān lái de
en: When did you move here?
why: A question that already has 什么时候 does not take 吗.

s: 我是昨天来了的。
s_py: wǒ shì zuó tiān lái le de
zh: 我是昨天来的。
py: wǒ shì zuó tiān lái de
en: I came yesterday.
why: 是…的 already places the event in the past, so 了 is not added inside it.

src_py: wǒ zuò dì tiě lái le
task: Stress how I came (it is already known that I am here).
zh: 我是坐地铁来的。
py: wǒ shì zuò dì tiě lái de
en: I came by subway.
why: The arrival is known, so the manner is stressed with 是 before 坐地铁 and 的 after 来, and 了 drops out.

q: 他明天___坐火车去上海。
zh: 他明天要坐火车去上海。
py: tā míng tiān yào zuò huǒ chē qù shàng hǎi
en: He is going to Shanghai by train tomorrow.
why: Tomorrow is the future, so 要 is correct and there is no 的. 刚 and 已经 are for things that have happened and 过 is an experience marker.

s: 我是下个月打算搬家的。
s_py: wǒ shì xià ge yuè dǎ suàn bān jiā de
zh: 我下个月打算搬家。
py: wǒ xià ge yuè dǎ suàn bān jiā
en: I plan to move house next month.
why: A plan for next month is not a known past event. Use plain word order with 打算, no 是…的.

s: 他是上个月回的来。
s_py: tā shì shàng ge yuè huí de lái
zh: 他是上个月回来的。
py: tā shì shàng ge yuè huí lái de
en: He came back last month.
why: 的 cannot split a verb from its 来. It goes after the whole verb 回来.

s: 这张桌子是我爸爸做的。
s_py: zhè zhāng zhuō zi shì wǒ bà ba zuò de
zh: 这张桌子是我爸爸做的。
py: zhè zhāng zhuō zi shì wǒ bà ba zuò de
en: My dad made this table.
why: This is correct. 是 + doer + verb + 的 says who made something that already exists, without any 被.

zh: 他打算下个月搬到新家。
py: tā dǎ suàn xià ge yuè bān dào xīn jiā
en: He plans to move to his new home next month.
why: A plan for next month uses 打算 and plain word order. Adding 是…的 would claim the move has already happened.

q: 我们是骑自行车去公园___。
zh: 我们是骑自行车去公园的。
py: wǒ men shì qí zì xíng chē qù gōng yuán de
en: We went to the park by bike.
why: The manner (骑自行车) is the stressed detail, so the sentence ends in 的 after 去公园. 着 and 过 cannot end a 是 sentence.

q: 这些花是在学校旁边的花店买___。
zh: 这些花是在学校旁边的花店买的。
py: zhè xiē huā shì zài xué xiào páng biān de huā diàn mǎi de
en: These flowers were bought at the flower shop next to the school.
why: The flowers are in front of us, so only the place is being told. 是 + place + 买 + 的 is the frame; 着 and 过 cannot end it.

q: 我们不是昨天买的票，___前天买的。
zh: 我们不是昨天买的票，是前天买的。
py: wǒ men bù shì zuó tiān mǎi de piào shì qián tiān mǎi de
en: We did not buy the tickets yesterday; we bought them the day before.
why: After denying one date, the right date is given with a positive 是…的 clause, so 是 must be there. 没 and 不 would negate again and 也 means also.

q: 我们是___这儿找李老师的，他在办公室吗？
zh: 我们是来这儿找李老师的，他在办公室吗？
py: wǒ men shì lái zhè r zhǎo lǐ lǎo shī de tā zài bàn gōng shì ma
en: We are here to see Teacher Li. Is he in his office?
why: Purpose is stressed with 来 + the action, and 来 is right because the speakers are already here. 去 would point away from here, 回 means going back.

src: 他搬到上海是因为工作。
src_py: tā bān dào shàng hǎi shì yīn wèi gōng zuò
task: Rewrite with 为了 and 是…的.
zh: 他是为了工作搬到上海的。
py: tā shì wèi le gōng zuò bān dào shàng hǎi de
en: He moved to Shanghai for work.
why: The purpose phrase 为了工作 follows 是 and 的 ends the verb phrase. 是因为 is replaced, not kept.

s: 我是上周在街上看见他的。
s_py: wǒ shì shàng zhōu zài jiē shàng kàn jiàn tā de
zh: 我是上周在街上看见他的。
py: wǒ shì shàng zhōu zài jiē shàng kàn jiàn tā de
en: I saw him on the street last week.
why: This is correct. With a pronoun object 的 goes at the very end. It may look odd because 的 usually follows the verb before a noun, but that applies only to noun objects.

s: 我下个星期坐火车去北京。
s_py: wǒ xià ge xīng qī zuò huǒ chē qù běi jīng
zh: 我下个星期坐火车去北京。
py: wǒ xià ge xīng qī zuò huǒ chē qù běi jīng
en: I am going to Beijing by train next week.
why: This is correct. Next week is future, so plain word order is right. Adding 是…的 here would be the mistake.

src_py: wǒ nǎi nai zuò le zhè xiē jiǎo zi
task: The dumplings are on the table. Stress that Grandma made them.
zh: 这些饺子是我奶奶做的。
py: zhè xiē jiǎo zi shì wǒ nǎi nai zuò de
en: My grandma made these dumplings.
why: Known dumplings become the topic and the doer gets 是. 的 sits after 做, or at the end if the object follows the verb.

src_py: tā zuó tiān huí jiā le
task: He is already home. Stress that it was yesterday.
zh: 他是昨天回家的。
py: tā shì zuó tiān huí jiā de
en: He came home yesterday.
why: Once the return is known, 是 goes before 昨天 and 的 ends the verb phrase. 了 is not kept inside 是…的.

src_py: tā zuò huǒ chē qù le shàng hǎi
task: Say he has gone to Shanghai, then add how he went with 是…的.
zh: 他去上海了是坐火车去的。
py: tā qù shàng hǎi le shì zuò huǒ chē qù de
en: He has gone to Shanghai; he went by train.
why: The trip is reported first with 了. Once it is known, the manner follows in a 是…的 clause. The two cannot share one clause.

src_py: wǒ lái xué zhōng wén
task: Say what you came for, using 是…的.
zh: 我是来学中文的。
py: wǒ shì lái xué zhōng wén de
en: I came to study Chinese.
why: Purpose is stressed with 是 + 来 + purpose, and 的 closes the phrase. Without 的 the sentence only says what you are doing.

src_py: tā shì shàng ge yuè dào de
task: Make it negative.
zh: 他不是上个月到的。
py: tā bù shì shàng ge yuè dào de
en: He did not arrive last month.
why: Negating 是…的 replaces 是 with 不是 and keeps 的. It denies the time, not the arrival itself.

src_py: tā shì zuò gōng gòng qì chē lái de
task: Ask how he came.
zh: 他是怎么来的？
py: tā shì zěn me lái de
en: How did he get here?
why: The question word 怎么 replaces the manner in the stressed slot and 的 stays. 他怎么来了 would ask a different question.

zh: 你是不是坐地铁来的？
py: nǐ shì bù shì zuò dì tiě lái de
en: Did you come by subway?
why: The yes/no form puts 是不是 where 是 would be, before the stressed manner. 的 still closes the verb phrase, and no 吗 is needed.

q: 这张桌子___上个星期在网上买的。
zh: 这张桌子是上个星期在网上买的。
py: zhè zhāng zhuō zi shì shàng ge xīng qī zài wǎng shàng mǎi de
en: This table was bought online last week.
why: The topic 这张桌子 is followed by 是 before the time phrase, with 的 at the end. 被 needs a doer straight after it, and 把 and 给 do not fit here.

q: 我妹妹昨天终于买___那条裙子，是在网上用半价买的。
zh: 我妹妹昨天终于买了那条裙子，是在网上用半价买的。
py: wǒ mèi mei zuó tiān zhōng yú mǎi le nà tiáo qún zi shì zài wǎng shàng yòng bàn jià mǎi de
en: My younger sister finally bought that skirt yesterday; she got it online at half price.
why: Finally buying the skirt is the news, so 了. The how and where are then added in a second clause with 是…的. 的 here would turn the first clause into a modifier with no main verb.

q: 他们是为了让孩子上好学校才搬到这个小区___。
zh: 他们是为了让孩子上好学校才搬到这个小区的。
py: tā men shì wèi le ràng hái zi shàng hǎo xué xiào cái bān dào zhè ge xiǎo qū de
en: They moved to this neighbourhood so that their child could go to a good school.
why: The stressed detail is the purpose (为了…), so the verb phrase ends in 的. 着 and 过 do not fit after 搬到 + place in a purpose sentence.

q: 我爸妈是二十年前在上海的一家小饭馆认识___。
zh: 我爸妈是二十年前在上海的一家小饭馆认识的。
py: wǒ bà mā shì èr shí nián qián zài shàng hǎi de yī jiā xiǎo fàn guǎn rèn shi de
en: My parents met in a small restaurant in Shanghai twenty years ago.
why: That they know each other is a given; the story fills in when and where. 是 + time/place + 认识 + 的 is the frame, and nothing else can close it.

q: 这件衣服___我买的，是我姐姐送给我的。
zh: 这件衣服不是我买的，是我姐姐送给我的。
py: zhè jiàn yī fu bù shì wǒ mǎi de shì wǒ jiě jie sòng gěi wǒ de
en: I did not buy this piece of clothing; my sister gave it to me.
why: The negative is 不是…的, which denies who did it. 没是 does not exist, bare 不 leaves no verb 是 for 的 to pair with, and 没有 changes the meaning.

zh: 你是在哪儿买的票？
py: nǐ shì zài nǎ r mǎi de piào
en: Where did you buy the ticket?
why: 是 comes before the stressed place 在哪儿. With a noun object, 的 can sit after the verb or at the end, or the object can become the topic at the front.

s: 我昨天买了一件很贵的外套，是在市中心的商场买的。
s_py: wǒ zuó tiān mǎi le yī jiàn hěn guì de wài tào shì zài shì zhōng xīn de shāng chǎng mǎi de
zh: 我昨天买了一件很贵的外套，是在市中心的商场买的。
py: wǒ zuó tiān mǎi le yī jiàn hěn guì de wài tào shì zài shì zhōng xīn de shāng chǎng mǎi de
en: I bought a very expensive coat yesterday; I got it at a mall in the city centre.
why: This is correct. The first clause reports a new purchase with 了, and the second gives the known purchase's place with 是…的.

q: 你是___到学校的？坐车还是走路？
zh: 你是怎么到学校的？坐车还是走路？
py: nǐ shì zěn me dào xué xiào de zuò chē hái shi zǒu lù
en: How did you get to school? Did you ride or walk?
why: The follow-up asks about ways of travelling, so the question word is 怎么 (how). 为什么 would ask for the reason and 什么 and 谁 do not fit the verb 到.

q: 他是___上海出生的，不是北京。
zh: 他是在上海出生的，不是北京。
py: tā shì zài shàng hǎi chū shēng de bù shì běi jīng
en: He was born in Shanghai, not Beijing.
why: The place of an event is introduced by 在. 从 would mean from, and 到 and 去 are movement words that cannot mark where someone was born.

zh: 我爷爷是昨天回来的。
py: wǒ yé ye shì zuó tiān huí lái de
en: My grandpa came back yesterday.
why: 是 stands before the time detail 昨天, and 的 comes last because 回来 ends in 来. 我爷爷昨天是回来的 puts 是 in the wrong slot.

zh: 这把伞不是在商店买的。
py: zhè bǎ sǎn bù shì zài shāng diàn mǎi de
en: This umbrella was not bought in a shop.
why: 不是 goes before the denied place phrase and 的 closes the verb 买. 是 must not be dropped in a negative.

zh: 他们是坐飞机到上海的。
py: tā men shì zuò fēi jī dào shàng hǎi de
en: They got to Shanghai by plane.
why: The manner 坐飞机 is stressed, so 是 goes before it and 的 comes after 到上海. 他们坐飞机是到上海的 would stress the wrong thing.

q: 他回家___，是坐公共汽车回去的。
zh: 他回家了，是坐公共汽车回去的。
py: tā huí jiā le shì zuò gōng gòng qì chē huí qù de
en: He has gone home; he went by bus.
why: The first clause reports a new event, which takes 了. The second clause then gives a detail of that event with 是…的. 的 would make both clauses detail clauses and 过 gives an ever-experience.

src: 我们是上个星期回老家的。
src_py: wǒ men shì shàng ge xīng qī huí lǎo jiā de
task: Say we plan to go back next week.
zh: 我们下个星期要回老家。
py: wǒ men xià ge xīng qī yào huí lǎo jiā
en: We are going back to our hometown next week.
why: A plan uses 要 and plain word order; 是…的 only covers events that are already over.

src_py: wǒ zuó tiān mǎi le zhè jiàn wài tào
task: The coat is hanging right there. Say it was bought yesterday.
zh: 这件外套是昨天买的。
py: zhè jiàn wài tào shì zuó tiān mǎi de
en: This coat was bought yesterday.
why: The coat is visible, so only the time is news: 是…的 replaces 了. 这件外套昨天买了 would report the purchase itself.

src_py: wǒ shì zuò fēi jī lái de
task: Make it negative.
zh: 我不是坐飞机来的。
py: wǒ bù shì zuò fēi jī lái de
en: I did not come by plane.
why: The negative is 不是 before the denied manner; 是 stays and 的 stays. 没 is not used and 是 cannot be dropped.

q: 我们是跟爷爷一起去超市___。
zh: 我们是跟爷爷一起去超市的。
py: wǒ men shì gēn yé ye yī qǐ qù chāo shì de
en: We went to the supermarket with Grandpa.
why: The trip is known; 跟爷爷一起 says with whom. After 是 + the stressed phrase, the verb phrase 去超市 must end in 的.

zh: 我是上个月看见他的。
py: wǒ shì shàng ge yuè kàn jiàn tā de
en: I saw him last month.
why: With a pronoun object, 的 goes last (看见他的). Putting 的 right after the verb is heard in casual speech but is not the standard order.

zh: 这个蛋糕是妈妈做的。
py: zhè ge dàn gāo shì mā ma zuò de
en: Mum made this cake.
why: The doer is stressed: 是 + 妈妈 + 做 + 的. The cake may be fronted as the topic or follow 的 as the object, but 是 always stays before the doer.

zh: 我是跟朋友一起去的。
py: wǒ shì gēn péng you yī qǐ qù de
en: I went with friends.
why: 是 goes right before the companion phrase, and the verb 去 is closed by 的. Ending on 去 without 的 would leave the pattern unfinished.

zh: 我妹妹到家了是坐出租车回来的。
py: wǒ mèi mei dào jiā le shì zuò chū zū chē huí lái de
en: My sister is home; she came back by taxi.
why: The first clause is news and takes 了. The second clause adds the manner with 是 + 坐出租车 + 回来 + 的. The two patterns do not mix in one clause.

q: 你是跟___去的医院？
zh: 你是跟谁去的医院？
py: nǐ shì gēn shéi qù de yī yuàn
en: Who did you go to the hospital with?
why: 跟 introduces a companion, so the question word must be a person, 谁. The question word sits in the stressed slot after 是.

zh: 是谁告诉你的？
py: shì shéi gào su nǐ de
en: Who told you?
why: 谁 is the stressed doer, so it follows 是 directly. 的 goes after the pronoun 你, or just after the verb in casual speech; it never comes first.

q: 我哥哥是三年前一个人去上海___，现在已经在那儿工作了。
zh: 我哥哥是三年前一个人去上海的，现在已经在那儿工作了。
py: wǒ gē ge shì sān nián qián yī ge rén qù shàng hǎi de xiàn zài yǐ jīng zài nà r gōng zuò le
en: My older brother went to Shanghai on his own three years ago, and he is already working there now.
why: The second clause gives the known outcome; the first fills in when and how he went. 是…的 supplies the detail and takes no 了 inside it.

q: 你今天怎么来___？我没看见你的车。
zh: 你今天怎么来的？我没看见你的车。
py: nǐ jīn tiān zěn me lái de wǒ méi kàn jiàn nǐ de chē
en: How did you get here today? I did not see your car.
why: Asking the manner of a known arrival needs 的 even with 是 dropped. 你怎么来了 would mean how come you are here, which does not match the question about the car.

s: 我们是坐地铁不来的。
s_py: wǒ men shì zuò dì tiě bù lái de
zh: 我们不是坐地铁来的。
py: wǒ men bù shì zuò dì tiě lái de
en: We did not come by subway.
why: The negation belongs in front of 是 (不是), not on the verb. 不来 turns it into not coming at all.

q: 他们是搬到这个城市以后才认识___，以前根本不认识。
zh: 他们是搬到这个城市以后才认识的，以前根本不认识。
py: tā men shì bān dào zhè ge chéng shì yǐ hòu cái rèn shi de yǐ qián gēn běn bù rèn shi
en: They only got to know each other after moving to this city; they did not know each other before.
why: The time of getting to know each other is the stressed detail: 是 + time clause + 才认识 + 的. 着 and 过 do not close this pattern.

src_py: xiǎo wáng gào su le wǒ
task: Stress that it was Xiao Wang who told me.
zh: 是小王告诉我的。
py: shì xiǎo wáng gào su wǒ de
en: It was Xiao Wang who told me.
why: The doer is stressed by putting 是 before it, and 的 goes after the pronoun 我. 了 is not kept.

q: 你们是什么时候搬到这个小区___？
zh: 你们是什么时候搬到这个小区的？
py: nǐ men shì shén me shí hou bān dào zhè ge xiǎo qū de
en: When did you move to this neighbourhood?
why: A past event with the time asked takes 是…的, and a question word makes a final 吗 impossible. 了 does not go after 是 + question word.

q: 我昨天买___一件外套，是在网上买的。
zh: 我昨天买了一件外套，是在网上买的。
py: wǒ zuó tiān mǎi le yī jiàn wài tào shì zài wǎng shàng mǎi de
en: I bought a coat yesterday; I bought it online.
why: A counted new object means the purchase is the news, so 了 follows 买. Only the next clause, about where, uses 是…的. 过 would mean I have bought one at some time.

q: 这个菜___我妈妈做的。
zh: 这个菜是我妈妈做的。
py: zhè ge cài shì wǒ mā ma zuò de
en: My mum made this dish.
why: To say who made a finished thing, put 是 before the doer. 被 is not used for plain English was-made-by, and 把 and 对 do not link a doer to a dish.

q: 我姐姐是昨天回家___。
zh: 我姐姐是昨天回家的。
py: wǒ jiě jie shì zuó tiān huí jiā de
en: My older sister came home yesterday.
why: Her coming home is known; 昨天 is the detail, so 是 comes before it and 的 closes the verb phrase. 过 would mean having done it at some point, 着 a continuing state.

q: 这双鞋你在哪儿买___？
zh: 这双鞋你在哪儿买的？
py: zhè shuāng xié nǐ zài nǎ r mǎi de
en: Where did you buy these shoes?
why: The shoes are known and the question is only about the place, so 的 closes the 是-less pattern. 了 would report a purchase and does not fit a fronted object.

q: 这张照片是在___拍的？看起来很漂亮。
zh: 这张照片是在哪儿拍的？看起来很漂亮。
py: zhè zhāng zhào piàn shì zài nǎ r pāi de kàn qǐ lái hěn piào liang
en: Where was this photo taken? It looks beautiful.
why: 在 must be followed by a place, so 哪儿 is the only fit. 谁, 怎么 and 什么时候 cannot follow 在 here.

q: 他不___为了钱才搬到这个城市的。
zh: 他不是为了钱才搬到这个城市的。
py: tā bù shì wèi le qián cái bān dào zhè ge chéng shì de
en: He did not move to this city for the money.
why: The negative needs 是 to pair with the final 的: 不是 + purpose + verb + 的. 不有, 不在 and 不要 are different words and change the meaning.

src_py: wǒ zài běi jīng xué zhōng wén
task: Say that it was in Beijing that I learned Chinese (是…的).
zh: 我是在北京学的中文。
py: wǒ shì zài běi jīng xué de zhōng wén
en: I learned Chinese in Beijing.
why: The place gets 是, and with a noun object 的 can follow the verb or end the sentence. The object may also be fronted as the topic.

q: 我爸爸是坐出租车来___。
zh: 我爸爸是坐出租车来的。
py: wǒ bà ba shì zuò chū zū chē lái de
en: My dad came by taxi.
why: Dad is already here, so only the manner is news: 是 + 坐出租车 + 来 + 的. 着 and 过 do not close a 是 sentence about a past trip.

src_py: zhè tiáo kù zi shì wǒ mǎi de
task: Make it negative.
zh: 这条裤子不是我买的。
py: zhè tiáo kù zi bù shì wǒ mǎi de
en: I did not buy these trousers.
why: 不是 goes before the denied doer and 的 stays after the verb. The negative cannot use 没.

src_py: nǐ shì zài nǎ r mǎi de
task: Say it more casually by dropping 是.
zh: 你在哪儿买的？
py: nǐ zài nǎ r mǎi de
en: Where did you buy it?
why: In questions 是 may be left out in speech, but 的 must stay. 你在哪儿买 without 的 loses the meaning of asking about a known purchase.

src_py: wǒ shì zuó tiān dào de
task: Ask the other person when they arrived.
zh: 你是什么时候到的？
py: nǐ shì shén me shí hou dào de
en: When did you arrive?
why: The question word 什么时候 replaces 昨天, directly after 是, and 的 stays. 你什么时候到了 would sound like asking when you will arrive.

q: 他不是昨天到___，是前天到的。
zh: 他不是昨天到的，是前天到的。
py: tā bù shì zuó tiān dào de shì qián tiān dào de
en: He did not arrive yesterday; he arrived the day before.
why: The correction denies the day, and both clauses end in 的. 过 and 着 cannot close a 是…的 clause.

s: 我爷爷是在上海出生的。
s_py: wǒ yé ye shì zài shàng hǎi chū shēng de
zh: 我爷爷是在上海出生的。
py: wǒ yé ye shì zài shàng hǎi chū shēng de
en: My grandpa was born in Shanghai.
why: This is correct. Being born is a past event that is known, and the place is the detail. English says was born, but Chinese still uses 是…的.

q: 这张照片是我去年___上海拍的。
zh: 这张照片是我去年在上海拍的。
py: zhè zhāng zhào piàn shì wǒ qù nián zài shàng hǎi pāi de
en: I took this photo in Shanghai last year.
why: The place where something was done is marked with 在. 从 and 往 are direction words that cannot go before a verb of taking a photo, and 对 does not mark a place.

q: 我们到家___，现在在吃饭。
zh: 我们到家了，现在在吃饭。
py: wǒ men dào jiā le xiàn zài zài chī fàn
en: We have got home and are eating now.
why: Arriving home is the new event being reported, so 了. 的 only works if the arrival is already known and a detail like time or manner is being given.

zh: 我们不是走路来的。
py: wǒ men bù shì zǒu lù lái de
en: We did not come on foot.
why: The negative is 不是 + manner + verb + 的. It denies the manner (we came some other way); 我们没走路来的 is a different sentence.

s: 他们是去年夏天在北京结婚过。
s_py: tā men shì qù nián xià tiān zài běi jīng jié hūn guò
zh: 他们是去年夏天在北京结婚的。
py: tā men shì qù nián xià tiān zài běi jīng jié hūn de
en: They got married in Beijing last summer.
why: The 是 sentence is closed by 的, not 过. 过 marks an experience and cannot end 是…的.

zh: 你是在哪家医院出生的？
py: nǐ shì zài nǎ jiā yī yuàn chū shēng de
en: Which hospital were you born in?
why: The question word phrase 在哪家医院 is the stressed place, so 是 is right before it. 出生 takes no object, so 的 stays at the end.

s: 我坐地铁来的。
s_py: wǒ zuò dì tiě lái de
zh: 我坐地铁来的。
py: wǒ zuò dì tiě lái de
en: I came by subway.
why: This is correct. 是 may be dropped in a statement but 的 stays. It may look incomplete without 是, but 的 carries the pattern.

s: 你是怎么来的？
s_py: nǐ shì zěn me lái de
zh: 你是怎么来的？
py: nǐ shì zěn me lái de
en: How did you get here?
why: This is correct. Asking about the manner of a known arrival takes 是…的 with 怎么 in the stressed slot. It does not need 吗 or 了.

zh: 我昨天去超市了。
py: wǒ zuó tiān qù chāo shì le
en: I went to the supermarket yesterday.
why: This reports a new event, not a detail of a known one, so it takes 了 and no 是…的. The time word may sit before or after the subject.

q: 我是在朋友的婚礼上第一次见到他___，那时候他还不会说中文。
zh: 我是在朋友的婚礼上第一次见到他的，那时候他还不会说中文。
py: wǒ shì zài péng you de hūn lǐ shàng dì yī cì jiàn dào tā de nà shí hou tā hái bù huì shuō zhōng wén
en: I first met him at a friend's wedding, when he could not yet speak Chinese.
why: The place and occasion of a past meeting is the stressed detail, and the pronoun object 他 means 的 comes last. 着 and 过 cannot end the pattern.

q: 你是坐地铁来的___坐公共汽车来的？
zh: 你是坐地铁来的还是坐公共汽车来的？
py: nǐ shì zuò dì tiě lái de hái shi zuò gōng gòng qì chē lái de
en: Did you come by subway or by bus?
why: A question that offers two choices uses 还是. 或者 is for statements, and 和 and 但是 do not join two alternatives in a question.

src: 他们是坐火车去北京的。
src_py: tā men shì zuò huǒ chē qù běi jīng de
task: Make it negative.
zh: 他们不是坐火车去北京的。
py: tā men bù shì zuò huǒ chē qù běi jīng de
en: They did not go to Beijing by train.
why: 不是 replaces 是 and denies the manner. 的 goes after 去, or after 北京 when a place object follows.

zh: 你是什么时候搬到这儿的？
py: nǐ shì shén me shí hou bān dào zhè r de
en: When did you move here?
why: The question word 什么时候 sits right after 是 as the stressed detail, and 的 comes last after 这儿. 吗 is not added to a question-word question.

zh: 我们明天坐地铁去。
py: wǒ men míng tiān zuò dì tiě qù
en: We are going by subway tomorrow.
why: Tomorrow is future, so this is plain word order with no 是 and no 的. The time word may come before or after the subject.

s: 他是什么时候到了？
s_py: tā shì shén me shí hou dào le
zh: 他是什么时候到的？
py: tā shì shén me shí hou dào de
en: When did he arrive?
why: Asking when a known arrival happened needs 的 at the end. 了 does not go after 是 + question word.

q: 这张画是我女儿画___，不是老师画的。
zh: 这张画是我女儿画的，不是老师画的。
py: zhè zhāng huà shì wǒ nǚ ér huà de bù shì lǎo shī huà de
en: My daughter drew this picture, not the teacher.
why: The doer is stressed with 是 and the verb closes with 的, just like the 的 in the contrasting clause. 着 and 过 cannot close this pattern.

s: 这个蛋糕被我姐姐做了。
s_py: zhè ge dàn gāo bèi wǒ jiě jie zuò le
zh: 这个蛋糕是我姐姐做的。
py: zhè ge dàn gāo shì wǒ jiě jie zuò de
en: My sister made this cake.
why: Chinese does not use 被 to say who made something. Use 是 + doer + verb + 的.

s: 这是谁拍的？
s_py: zhè shì shéi pāi de
zh: 这是谁拍的？
py: zhè shì shéi pāi de
en: Who took this?
why: This is correct. 这 stays as the subject and 是 must be kept after it. 谁 is the stressed doer and 的 ends the verb phrase.

zh: 我不是为了赚钱来这儿的。
py: wǒ bù shì wèi le zhuàn qián lái zhè r de
en: I did not come here to make money.
why: 不是 goes before the denied purpose 为了赚钱, and 的 stays at the very end after 来这儿. 来的这儿 would split the verb from its place.

q: 这个蛋糕是___做的？很好吃。
zh: 这个蛋糕是谁做的？很好吃。
py: zhè ge dàn gāo shì shéi zuò de hěn hǎo chī
en: Who made this cake? It is delicious.
why: The cake is already made and the question is about the maker, so 谁 goes between 是 and 做的. 怎么 would ask how it was made.

q: 我们是在地铁上遇见他___。
zh: 我们是在地铁上遇见他的。
py: wǒ men shì zài dì tiě shàng yù jiàn tā de
en: We met him on the subway.
why: With a pronoun object 的 goes at the very end: 遇见他的. 着 and 过 do not close a 是 sentence about a finished meeting.

q: 我们明年___搬到新家，现在还在找房子。
zh: 我们明年要搬到新家，现在还在找房子。
py: wǒ men míng nián yào bān dào xīn jiā xiàn zài hái zài zhǎo fáng zi
en: We are moving into a new home next year; we are still looking for a place now.
why: Next year is future, so plain 要 + verb is used. 是…的 is for events that are over. 刚 and 已经 describe the past and clash with 明年.

q: 桌上有一杯热茶，是谁给我倒___？
zh: 桌上有一杯热茶，是谁给我倒的？
py: zhuō shàng yǒu yī bēi rè chá shì shéi gěi wǒ dào de
en: There is a cup of hot tea on the table. Who poured it for me?
why: The cup of tea is visible, so the event is known and only the doer is asked about: 是谁…的. 着 and 过 do not close this question.

q: 这个字我是___手机查的。
zh: 这个字我是用手机查的。
py: zhè ge zì wǒ shì yòng shǒu jī chá de
en: I looked this character up on my phone.
why: The detail is the means, so 用 (using) fits before 手机. 在 would make the phone a place, and 跟 and 对 do not take a tool.

src_py: wǒ zuó tiān kàn jiàn le tā
task: Stress that it was yesterday (是…的).
zh: 我是昨天看见他的。
py: wǒ shì zuó tiān kàn jiàn tā de
en: I saw him yesterday.
why: The time becomes the stressed detail; with a pronoun object 的 goes at the very end. 了 is dropped.

q: 这本书___朋友送给我的。
zh: 这本书是朋友送给我的。
py: zhè běn shū shì péng you sòng gěi wǒ de
en: A friend gave me this book.
why: Stress the giver with 是 + doer + 的. 被 and 让 would need a different structure, and 由 does not combine with a giving verb here.

src: 我们在小区门口遇到了李老师。
src_py: wǒ men zài xiǎo qū mén kǒu yù dào le lǐ lǎo shī
task: Stress where we met him (是…的).
zh: 我们是在小区门口遇到李老师的。
py: wǒ men shì zài xiǎo qū mén kǒu yù dào lǐ lǎo shī de
en: We ran into Teacher Li at the entrance of the compound.
why: The place gets 是 and 了 is dropped. A noun object lets 的 sit after the verb or at the end, and the object can also be fronted.

q: 我___是在家吃的饭，是在奶奶家吃的。
zh: 我不是在家吃的饭，是在奶奶家吃的。
py: wǒ bù shì zài jiā chī de fàn shì zài nǎi nai jiā chī de
en: I did not eat at home; I ate at Grandma's.
why: The negative of 是…的 is 不是, denying the place. 没是 is not a word, and 别 and 很 do not make sense before 是 here.

zh: 我们是来看奶奶的。
py: wǒ men shì lái kàn nǎi nai de
en: We came to see Grandma.
why: Purpose is stressed with 是 + 来 + action, and 的 closes the sentence. 我们来是看奶奶的 puts 是 in the wrong slot.
